packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

reader: Codex isolated image-only reader (model version not exposed)
text:
UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING. No candidate identification supplied or exposed. I cannot recover a dependable consecutive Latin quotation from these images.

Layout: large irregular, mostly blank surviving sheet with major losses. The small surviving text block is at upper right in image-001.jpg and upper left in image-002.jpg, upright in both. The main hand is very cursive, brown, and heavily abbreviated. image-001 also has a denser small-hand block above the larger writing, faint isolated writing in the blank area at left, and pen flourishes. No visible colored rubric, enlarged decorative initial, running title, or clear underlining. The physical edges remove portions of many lines. The images appear to show opposite faces, rather than two adjacent complete pages.

Native inspection crops, no rotation/scaling: crop-001.jpg from image-001.jpg (3639 x 3495), box (2620,0,3639,1817); crop-002.jpg from image-002.jpg (same dimensions), box (0,279,1164,1782). These are overlapping detail views of the originals, not additional text. crop-002 line numbers count the first visible main-text line as L1; these also match the surviving main text lines in image-002.

Small provisional readings from image-002, not a coherent reconstructed passage:
crop-002.jpg L1: [lost left] [illegible] qui [illegible]
crop-002.jpg L2: [lost left] [illegible] et no(n)? [illegible]
crop-002.jpg L3: fuit? [illegible] in ista [illegible]
crop-002.jpg L4: [lost left] [illegible] Solutio? [illegible] dicit?
crop-002.jpg L5: duplex? e(st)? [illegible] fuit? [illegible]
crop-002.jpg L6: [illegible]
crop-002.jpg L7: [illegible] q(ui)? [illegible]
crop-002.jpg L8: [lost left] [illegible] [hole] [illegible] [lost right]
crop-002.jpg L9: [illegible] [hole] et [illegible] [lost right]
crop-002.jpg L10: [illegible] sub? [illegible] [lost right]

image-001 selected block: the smaller top writing and the larger writing below it have different baselines and may be separate notes; a single line count through both would be misleading. In the larger block, repeated strings seem to read “qui fuit” / “qui sunt”, but even these are uncertain. No longer span is responsibly recoverable. I do not turn these fragments into grammatical sentences.

Limits: severe lacunae, fading, very compressed abbreviation, and possible differing text hands. Most surviving writing remains unread. No attribution or rubric wording recovered. This packet needs a reader practiced in this cursive hand; sharpening or a closer crop alone will not restore the missing parchment. The cropped images already retain the available native pixels. None of the isolated words above should be used as a positive identification without rechecking the image. This is an unverified reading, not an expert transcription.
